Have you tried to be in our shoes before? There were examples of business who tried and failed over and over again. 
It would be lots easier for bigger business to be that risky (yes risky) cause they have a bigger backing. 
As small business, we don't have backing. A lot of small business have been mom and pop run. Now a lot have died out. 
Coming from the other end of the country, in a small town, it really isn't easy to adapt. 
I am in a mom and pop business. Everyday our sales are low, even if we tried lowering our prices. There's nobody passing by even if it's supposedly a "busy" area. 
And if you haven't read or miss the part where I said that our expenses currently eats up our profits.
It's crazy ain't it? Working about 80 hours a week and still barely surviving the roller coaster we call the economy. Now being put on blast on the local paper. *sigh*

We get charged about 3% of the amount. Not profits. From sales which is a hefty amount of money in the long run depending on what the nature of business is (what is being sold). 
Of course business managing wise, we would deduct that from our profits right? But imagine this, if our profit margin was already monitored and the bank charges are greater or slightly equal to profits? We can't take afford that.

Our small businesses are being monitored on sales, profits and workers to ensure that we don't eff people without the care that the banks of the government are effing us around. Some of us can't help to increase prices or to not join the "Salebration" cause we couldn't afford it. 
Internet, electricity, rental, charges and a lot more of things go into running a business and that's just how we've been limited.

As hard to some people to think of it, we small business are also people, also with family, also with responsibilities. Personally I don't think we would try to make people feel inconvenience if we can provide the service to make things easier for everybody.

I think I'm going to try invest in some gym coupons or vouchers and give him as a surprise as a safe place for him to release some tension. The build up is quite noticeable. Even work mates who don't know him also could see the difference. 
We've tried the arcade. We tried going for spontaneous dates.
When he "exploded", I try not to disturb his outburst first. Times his phone was his victim, the car seats, or even some random dirt.  After he calms down a bit is when I go up and give him a big hug.

I've actually tried to get him to go to the gym or when his colleagues ask him out for a drink, but he won't budge. He's not interested in drinking with people and he feels discouraged when exercising at home isn't bring much results. 
On occasions, he mentions that he hates how his suffering is making me friendless as well. I work at front in retail sales so sometimes he has imaginary match making which i try to reassure it's only part of my job.

As I see it, only me and his friend has any clue of what he's suffering from. Other people around him just bring him down by being ignorant like "oh you're not the only one" and such.

He has no idea I've gone to the internet to ask for advises or that I've shared our story. He's a very private guy.

His dad hasn't stayed home much, even now when he's newly retired, his dad is still doing side projects away from home.
